title: Elijah will turn children’s hearts to their fathers before the Lord comes
setting: Section 2 is not a separate revelation text but an excerpt from Joseph Smith’s history. It records words Joseph reported hearing from a heavenly messenger on the night of 21 September 1823, when he was 17. The visit took place in the Smith family’s log home near Palmyra, New York. The official heading identifies the messenger as Moroni, the last keeper of the records that became the Book of Mormon. The messenger quoted Malachi 4:5–6 in a form that differs from the King James Bible. Joseph’s history was written from 1838 on, and these verses joined the Doctrine and Covenants in 1876.
summary: The messenger speaks for the Lord in three short verses. First, the Lord will reveal the priesthood by the hand of Elijah the prophet. This will happen before the great and dreadful day of the Lord. Elijah will plant in the children’s hearts the promises made to the fathers. Then the hearts of the children will turn to their fathers. If this did not happen, the whole earth would be utterly wasted at the Lord’s coming.

contextNote.title: What turns the children’s hearts
contextNote.text: In the King James Bible, Malachi says Elijah will turn hearts between fathers and children. Verse 2 adds a step before the turning. Elijah will first “plant in the hearts of the children” the promises made to the fathers. The children turn because those promises have been placed in them. Verse 1 ties this work to priesthood revealed by Elijah’s hand. Verse 3 gives the stakes: without it, the earth would be “utterly wasted” at the Lord’s coming. Here, turning the heart means taking the fathers’ promises as one’s own.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for section 2 teaches that the Lord sent Elijah to turn our hearts to our ancestors. Which “promises made to the fathers” in verse 2 might you trace in your own family’s history?
reviewNote: Read all 3 verses. Official heading gives the Smith log home at Palmyra, evening of 21 September 1823, and names Moroni. No JSP revelation document exists; the source is page 5 of the 1839 history draft (James Mulholland’s hand), which contains the Elijah quotation. That draft names the messenger “Nephi”; a later redaction changed it to Moroni as a clerical error. The 1876 date of inclusion in the D&C is from general knowledge, not the pages read. The log home stood near the Palmyra–Manchester line; I used palmyra as the heading does. Fact-check 2026-10-12: setting now attributes the messenger's visit to Joseph's report rather than stating it as fact.
